semantic_changes: Construct events now carry local_id in addition to mode, so their admissions can be correlated.
A second case pair with MaxAppendEntries=1 and 200 committed entries above the snapshot is added, with an off control at the same scale, so the trigger no longer depends on an entry gap above 8192.

scope.description: One node (LocalID A) constructed in four configurations from per-mode in-memory stores: a version-1 snapshot at index 1000 with configuration {A} plus committed LogCommand entries above it, with the commit-tracking store reporting the log's last index as commit index. Cases: 9000 entries with default MaxAppendEntries 64, feature off and on; 200 entries with MaxAppendEntries 1, feature off and on.
assumptions: The fixture (snapshot, entries, staged commit index) is supplied by the harness; it is the restart shape a node that ran with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled can reach, with the commit index persisted atomically with the entries by the store contract.
Batches are derived as ceil(entries above the snapshot / MaxAppendEntries) and emitted as an operand rather than asserted from a constant.

Non-return is evaluated by constructing in a goroutine and waiting 5s; each feature-on case has a feature-off control over the identical fixture and store objects, so fixture size, store speed and FSM speed are excluded as causes.
The feature-on instance that does not return cannot be shut down; its goroutine is abandoned when the test process exits.
excluded: No on-disk store, no live cluster and no crash path is exercised.
The stalled constructor is not resumed and no timeout or external supervision is modelled.

basis.prefix: Per case the harness builds fresh InmemTransport("A"), InmemStore (stable), InmemCommitTrackingStore (logs) and InmemSnapshotStore (snapshots); writes a version-1 snapshot at index 1000, term 1 with configuration {A} at configuration index 1 and closes the sink; stores the case's LogCommand entries at indices 1001.. in batches of 256; and calls logs.StageCommitIndex(last index). It emits a 'fixture' event with the case operands (mode, snapshot index, log last index, stored commit index, entries above the snapshot, MaxAppendEntries, batches required, observation window), then builds Config from DefaultConfig() with LocalID "A", the case's MaxAppendEntries, a null logger and RestoreCommittedLogs from the case, and calls NewRaft(conf, probeFSM, logs, stable, snaps, trans) in a goroutine. A 'construct' event reports mode, local_id, newraft_returned and, when the constructor returned, last applied index, queued FSM batches and the observed FSM mutation channel capacity. Case order is replay_off, replay_on, replay_off_small_batches, replay_on_small_batches, so the event order is fixture, construct, fixture, construct, fixture, construct, fixture, construct; the probe FSM discards applied entries and accepts the snapshot bytes.
basis.responsibility: hashicorp/raft NewRaft startup path: restoreFromCommittedLogs replays committed entries through processLogs into fsmMutateCh before the constructor starts the only consumer, runFSM.

comparisons.description: With the replay enabled over 141 batches, construction should return within the observation window.
Control: the identical 9000-entry fixture with the feature off should construct normally.
Control operand: without the replay the FSM is not advanced past the snapshot, so the comparison concerns the replay rather than the fixture.
With the replay enabled and MaxAppendEntries 1, 200 entries already exceed the 128-slot channel; construction should still return within the window.
Control at the same scale: the 200-entry MaxAppendEntries=1 fixture with the feature off should construct normally.

knowledge.assertion: restoreFromCommittedLogs calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil) before the configuration scan and before background goroutines start

before.description: A single node (LocalID A) constructed in two modes from the same in-memory stores: a version-1 snapshot at index 1000 with configuration {A} and a log of 9000 committed LogCommand entries above it (indices 1001..10000), with the commit-tracking store reporting commit index 10000; RestoreCommittedLogs off versus on, with normal initialization in both cases.
assumptions: The fixture is supplied by the harness (snapshot, 9000 entries, staged commit index); it is the restart-shaped state a node running with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled can reach, with the commit index persisted atomically with the log entries by the store contract.

The number of batches the replay produces is derived from MaxAppendEntries (64) and the entries above the snapshot (9000), giving 141 batches, and is emitted as an operand rather than asserted from a constant.
Non-return is evaluated by constructing in a goroutine and waiting 5s; the control uses the identical fixture with the feature off, so a slow fixture, slow store or slow FSM is excluded as the cause.
The feature-on node that never returns cannot be shut down; its goroutine is abandoned when the test process exits.
excluded: No on-disk store is exercised; the in-memory CommitTrackingLogStore is used.
The blocked constructor is not resumed, so no recovery path after the stall is observed.
